stages.description: The same onboarding ask, run through a spec layer. Intent is captured in a PRD with acceptance criteria, decomposed into a phased plan, and tracked in a YAML progress file the agent orchestra reads instead of guesses. The delta from Stage 1 is not speed for its own sake; it is that the work is legible to the next session.

steps.description: Opus reads frontmatter, not source. Executors get only their phase context.
steps.label: Orchestrator delegates by batch

agents.content:
Orchestration tier
  opus-orchestrator
    Reads: YAML frontmatter only (~2KB)
    Writes: batch dispatch + per-task context bundles
    Never reads: source files, full plan body

Execution tier (fan-out, parallel)
  ui-engineer (x3, one per task)
    Context: only this task's spec, only this screen's tokens
    Authority: Mode C (Autonomous Sprint) - clear intent, low blast radius
    Output: PR draft with evidence (screenshot + a11y scan)

Note: Progressive disclosure. No executor ever loads the
full plan or the PRD body; both are referenced by path.

steps.description: Deterministic operations get scripts, not agents. The intelligence budget is for judgment.
steps.label: Scripts for bookkeeping

agents.content:
Rule of thumb
  Use agents for judgment. Use scripts for bookkeeping.
  If the operation is deterministic, it does not need a model.

Replaced by scripts (per-call cost)
  update-status.py             ~50 tokens   (vs ~25,000 via agent)
  update-batch.py              ~80 tokens
  validate-phase-completion.py ~60 tokens
  query_artifacts.py           ~40 tokens

At 175+ active progress folders, this is the difference
between economically viable and not.
agents.title: When not to use an agent
